Abercrombie.notes: Bad. Even for low-oil purposes, which monitors (BMs) aren't used often for, Erebus is better among BMs.

Admiral Nakhimov.notes: One of the highest damage ships against medium armor, Nakhimov also has good damage against heavy armor enemies. When she launches an airstrike, she slows the enemies from 1.5s after her airstrike to 6.5s after. If the enemy is slowed by another Northern Parliament ship, then the period from 1.5s to 4.0s becomes a freeze. Nakhimov also gains +40% crit damage against enemies slowed by other NP ships, which is worth about 10% more damage. This makes her somewhat dependent on being run with another Northern Parliament ship that can slow enemies (usually Soyuz or Moskva). These tiers and damage ratings assume that there is no such slow in the fleet. See Nakhimov's pairing for an idea of how she performs with a good Northern Parliament ship who has a slow.

When Admiral Nakhimov launches an airstrike, she slows the enemies from 1.5s after her airstrike to 6.5s after. If the enemy is slowed by another Northern Parliament ship, then the period from 1.5s to 4.0s becomes a freeze. Nakhimov also gains +40% crit damage against enemies slowed by other NP ships, and this is worth about 10% more damage. Thus, her tiers and damage ratings assume that Moskva's permanent or Soyuz's 6 second slow is active for the whole period from 1.5s after Nakhimov's air strike until Nakhimov's payload hits. For the Offense Buff, she is credited with a freeze, but she only turns slow into freeze.

Admiral Zenker.notes: Standard top-level gold BB for 2025, less personal dmg than top gold BBs but has solid buffs.

Akagi.notes: A mediocre gold CV. If you really want her, wait until you're further along into the game when you can farm her and Kaga efficiently. Not assumed in these ratings, but she can be paired with Kaga or Kaga (BB) to make Akagi as strong as Akagi μ at the cost of an extra fleet slot.

Akagi μ.notes: Assume there are 3 muse ships in the fleet for 30% AVI. Ships can use Cosmic Kicks or Celestial Body to be considered as muse ships.

Akagi-chan.notes: One-time barrage requires 3 IJN, but it's not too important.

Akane Shinjo.notes: Her summon may draw or block a little fire, otherwise she's just decent pure damage.

Akashi.notes: Minor heals both inside and outside battle, and +1 ammo is very nice for mob.

Alabama.notes: A solid battleship for new players. She prefers to be in the mob fleet to ramp up damage but also does acceptable damage against single bosses.

Albion.notes: Assume there are 3 Royal Navy ships for 10% AVI.

Alsace.notes: One of the best all around rainbow BBs in the game currently. She has good damage output against all armor types with a preload (however her damage on a per-salvo basis is somewhat weaker compared to other rainbow BBs) and she’s one of the few BBs with salvo capacity +1 so she isn't affected by absolute cooldowns, making her quicker to reload her main guns in practice compared to other BBs. She also inflicts a 12% damage debuff on a priority enemy for 10 seconds. She also has a zombie heal when one of the ships in your fleet falls below 30% HP. Alsace doesn't have any real weaknesses per se but she’s not the absolute best at any one thing but early damage.

Alvitr.notes: Has a focused single-"shell" barrage, so a miss or a shield and her damage drops significantly.

Amagi.notes: Prefers 4 IJN ships, not assumed here.

Amagi(CV).notes: Amagi(CV) buffs all Sakura Empire torpedoes, including those from torpedo bombers, by 15%. This focus on TBs skews her against heavy armor bosses. Although she can do damage solo, she prefers to be paired with other Sakura Empire CV(s) to buff their TBs and receive their buffs. She also applies permanent debuffs stacking up to -9% stats to enemies, and these stats improve your fleet's offense by a slight amount and survivability by more. Put Amagi not in the flagship position to squeeze 0.5% more damage out of her distance skill.

Assumed to be with Shinano or Hakuhou. Amagi(CV) buffs all Sakura Empire torpedoes, including those from torpedo bombers, by 15%. This focus on TBs skews her against heavy armor bosses. She also applies permanent debuffs stacking up to -9% stats to enemies, and these stats improve your fleet's offense by a slight amount and survivability by more. Put Amagi not in the flagship position to squeeze 0.5% more damage out of her distance skill.

An Shan.notes: Not assumed, but can buff An Shan class.

Andrea Doria.notes: Has a small buff for Sardegna Empire ships and prefers to have another Sardegna BB in the fleet. Assume that she is buffing several Sardegna ships.

Andrea Doria META.notes: Assuming there is another META ship for +10% dmg.

Anniversary Kizuna AI.notes: Not assumed, but requires another Kizuna AI ship for Assault Carrier.

Aquila.notes: Aquila can be run in one of 2 configurations, a preload damage dealer mode (dive bomber in her second slot) or healer mode (fighter in her second slot). Her preload mode is pretty useless for endgame content, so for the most part, she will be run as a secondary healer. But when you do use her as a preloader, Aquila is good for farming easy battles fast, especially in Operation Siren where her oil cost does not matter.

Aquila can be run in one of 2 configurations, a preload damage dealer mode (dive bomber in her second slot) or healer mode (fighter in her second slot). Her preload mode is pretty useless for endgame content, so for the most part, she will be run as a secondary healer. Her total healing in comparison to other healers is a bit low, so it’s best to pair her with another healer like Unicorn.

Aquila can be run in one of 2 configurations, a preload damage dealer mode (dive bomber in her second slot) or healer mode (fighter in her second slot). Her preload mode is pretty useless for endgame content, so for the most part, she will be run as a secondary healer. Her total healing in comparison to other healers is a bit low, so it’s best to pair her with another healer like Unicorn. She has excellent synergy with Musashi, who can tank damage for the main fleet while Aquila’s heals and barriers can keep her healthy.

Arizona META.notes: Although the game says Arizona META's Jamming FIeld slows enemies by 80%, this is bugged to only slow by 50%. However, her very presence still eliminates 99% of Bombing Ships without even needing to shoot them because Bombing Ships self-destruct 5 seconds after spawning. Arizona META also has a large timeable one-time debuff for EX if you left her at level 1 for some reason.

Ark Royal.notes: Without her retrofit, Ark Royal loses a small AA debuff and minimal damage. Her main use of a strong 60% slow with very generous timing still applies.
Strong 60% slow with very generous timing. But it's not a freeze.

Arkhangelsk.notes: Assumes there are 3 Royal Navy or Northern Parliament ships for 15% FP.

August von Parseval.notes: August von Parseval is a decent gold carrier and one of the few ships in the game with the ability to freeze enemies in place. While there are better freezers out there, namely Implacable, AvP is still one of the most cost effective options as she doesn't require rainbow Bulins. If you don't have any ships who can freeze yet, AvP is a solid pick up.

BLACK★ROCK SHOOTER.notes: Generic good new gold BB/BC for 2025.

Bataan.notes: Should use F6F Hellcat when not using rocket fighters.

Bismarck.notes: Assumed to be buffing multiple KMS ships. So Bismarck is still bad unless the buffed ships are super strong.

Bismarck Zwei.notes: One of the best all-around rainbow BBs in the game currently. She has good damage output against all armor types on top of a 3 second black hole which can pull enemies together and act as a short freeze. The duration of the black hole is a bit on the short side though so if you want to take full advantage if it, your syncing needs to be very tight. Even with the best sync, the black hole would only help about half of the volleys in a triple BB fleet. Other than that, she doesn't have any real weaknesses, but she’s not the absolute best at any one thing. Although not reflected in her ratings, she can also run the auxiliary Certificate of Sponsorship which reduces the Out of Ammo debuff for your main fleet by 15%, useful when getting the third star in campaign.

Bois Belleau.notes: First airstrike is staggered, but further ones may be close to Unicorn. Prefers USS or Iris plane.

Centaur.notes: Assumes there are 3 Royal Navy ships for 10% more damage. Delayed slow. Needs to launch air strike before other main fleet ships.

Chihaya Kisaragi.notes: Not assumed because there's no good candidate, but an iM@S pairing gives a bonus.

Chitose.notes: Not assumed, but can sortie with another IJN CVL to double her barrage damage. Needs to launch airstrike before other main fleet ships to buff them.

Chiyoda.notes: Not assumed, but can sortie with another IJN CVL to double her barrage damage.

Chkalov.notes: Slow is only 3 seconds. Expensive to equip with 2 Tenrai's.

Clemenceau.notes: Requires various MNF ships. Assumes there is a Vichya vanguard ship and an Iris Orthodoxy gear.

Colorado.notes: Without her retrofit, she's just a mediocre Purple BB.
Assumes there is another BB for 12% FP and HIT.

Constellation.notes: Requires enemy to have lower speed than her.

Cowpens.notes: Cowpens has extremely good damage output for a healer, making her one of the best healers in the game. Her heals scale with her own max HP rather than the target’s, which makes her better at healing low HP ships like DDs and CLs but worse for main fleet ships, CAs, and CBs. She’s a very useful ship to have for all campaign chapters.

Daisen.notes: Daisen offers high damage for a gold BB, but her specialty is healing the vanguard when her airplane is shot down. In the main campaign, that can only happen in Chapter 13 and higher, and it happens inconsistently since Daisen usually kills the enemy AA ship before her airplane gets in range. Her Fate Simulation gives +9% single-target damage.

Duke of York.notes: Requires high-damage (UR) teammates to be good. Requires faster gun/radar to fire before said rainbow BB teammates.

Dunkerque META.notes: Preload but only 2 MGM. Small heal if multiple enemies.

Elise.notes: Elise buffs other main fleet ships by 5% damage and 10% FP or AVI stat. If there is another Venus Vacation ship, then she does about 3% more damage. She likes to expose herself, which could be bad in campaign or Challenge Mode.

Enterprise.notes: One of the best main fleet ships a new player is likely to get. For an average 70% proc rate, her damage sits at the high end for a gold CV. If you get lucky with 100% proc rate on her skill, she can match the damage of some rainbow CVs. She will fall off with time as you get ships that are able to match or exceed her damage output consistently, but there are few ships with better damage when you're new.

Essex.notes: Without her retrofit, Essex is a mediocre gold CV.

Relative to other rainbow CVs, Essex is a jack of all trades, master of none. She doesn't really have any strong synergies, but on the bright side, that means she fits well in any fleet as a transitional option. Although not assumed for these ratings, she slightly prefers to be with Eagle Union carriers for 5% AVI each. She is also one of the best support fleet carriers in late campaign. Note that her retrofit is VERY expensive.

Being in a fleet with Kearsarge, Yorktown II, and/or Lexington II massively buffs Essex but limits her to light armor bosses. In such a fleet, Essex only does damage and doesn't buff the fleet. That, combined with her lower anti-light damage relative to other Eagle Union rainbow CVs, makes her a transitional option. Note that her retrofit is VERY expensive.

Flandre.notes: Alsace at home. High gold BB level for 80s or 90s bossing.

Formidable.notes: Freeze is hard to use. Needs HMS gear.

Formidable μ.notes: Assumes there are 3 muse ships for a preload. Ships can equip Cosmic Kicks or Celestial Body to be considered as muse ships.

Francesco Caracciolo.notes: Heals herself and has decent damage, but 80% barrage is inconsistent.

Franklin.notes: About equal to 70% proc Enterprise in bossing. Assumes there is another Eagle Union main fleet ship for 10% damage.

Friedrich der Große.notes: One of the oldest rainbows in the game, and unfortunately it shows. She’s the weakest of the rainbow BBs except Vanguard in damage across all 3 armor types, and she doesn’t have any equivalent to Vanguard’s massive damage buffs and debuff to compensate. And to top it all off, to reach her damage potential as shown in these ratings, she needs to consistently take damage and/or have enemies nearby to proc her proximity barrage. Her screen-wide barrages do still make her an above average choice for W14, but even there she has been powercrept pretty hard.

Fritz Rumey.notes: Arguably the most flexible of the rainbow carriers, she is excellent against light and medium armor bosses thanks to her ability to equip 8 fighters (or 4 fighters and 4 Skyraiders). This also enables her to more easily get off 4 airstrikes in 80 seconds META showdowns compared to other carriers without gimping her damage too much. Her main weakness is that she’s more reliant on having good equipment (even compared to other carriers), and getting HVARcats, Skyraiders, and La-9s in quantity isn't that easy. She's also the best carrier for W15 and W16 support fleets.

Fubuki (Senran Kagura).notes: Various minor buffs. Barrage favors heavy armor.

Fusou.notes: Fully retrofitting Fusou and Yamashiro makes them much weaker. But they're bottom tier with or without retrofit. If you want maximum performance from them, retrofit until the Modernization node, do not complete Modernization. For collection percentage or historical reasons, just complete the retrofit.

Gangut.notes: Assumed to be buffing multiple SN ships. Augment is a decent improvement but she's still very bad.

Gangut META.notes: Will not kill 3 every salvo in higher chapters. So alternate slow and fast, but bad AA and low HP make her a poor choice. The damage rating of 2 assumes ST bossing without mobs.

Ganj-i-Sawai.notes: Does not have access to good guns and auxiliaries. Assumes there is another Tempesta ship for better healing.

Gascogne.notes: Has a wide barrage every 15s, though it lands at a specific depth so can't hit enemies that are too close or too far.

Gascogne μ.notes: Assumed to be buffing multiple muse ships.

Georgia.notes: 10% bonus vs CV/CVL. 20% bonus vs CA/CB/BB/BC/BBV, which is assumed in medium and heavy dmg.

Glorious META.notes: Glorious META REQUIRES an enemy with high-damage hits so that she can get at least 20 marks. She beats rainbow CVs if the battle is short enough for only one airstrike, but she is not good for EX because your vanguard needs to be hit too many times.

Gneisenau META.notes: Pick a KMS CL gun with 45 FP.

Golden Darkness.notes: Has rainbow BB-level gun efficiency, but suffers from low RLD and need to fire first.

Graf Zeppelin.notes: Assumes there are 3 Iron Blood ships for 15% AVI. Assumes she equipped an Iron Blood plane for 30% efficiency for all slots.

Hakuhou.notes: Hakuhou has top anti-heavy damage but no offensive fleet buffs. She also does about 9% more damage for every other Sakura Empire main fleet ship who reloads at roughly the same time as her. These ratings assume that there is one other Sakura Empire main fleet ship. Vanguard ships in the fleet enjoy up to 7% damage reduction, with DD/CL main guns reaching the 7% easily. She requires a Sakura Empire TB in her first slot for bossing against all armor types.

Hakuhou has top anti-heavy damage but no offensive fleet buffs. She also does about 9% more damage for every other Sakura Empire main fleet ship who reloads at roughly the same time as her. Pairing her with Shinano or Amagi(CV) forms a top anti-heavy fleet. Vanguard ships in the fleet enjoy up to 7% damage reduction, with DD/CL main guns reaching the 7% easily. She requires a Sakura Empire TB in her first slot for bossing against all armor types.
Note: When this ship is sortied with Amagi CV, the latter's damage buff to torpedoes from Sakura Empire ships makes converging torpedo bombers better than BF-109Gs against medium armor (assuming they hit the boss reliably) and parallel torpedo bombers relatively better than dive bombers in campaign in their flexible slots.

Hakuryuu.notes: Like Essex, Hakuryuu is a jack of all trades, master of none relative to other rainbow ships. She doesn't really have any strong synergies, but on the bright side, that means she fits well in any fleet as a transitional option. After fate simulation, she needs a Sakura Empire gear or ally. Before fate simulation, the requirement is stricter. Assume that she has a Sakura Empire plane or another Sakura ship.

Since Hakuryuu is the worst Sakura Empire rainbow CV for bossing, she can pair or be carried by Shinano or Amagi(CV) before you get the better ones. Like Essex, Hakuryuu is a jack of all trades, master of none relative to other rainbow ships. She doesn't really have any strong synergies, but on the bright side, that means she fits well in any fleet as a transitional option.
Note: When this ship is sortied with Amagi CV, the latter's damage buff to torpedoes from Sakura Empire ships makes converging torpedo bombers better than BF-109Gs against medium armor (assuming they hit the boss reliably) and parallel torpedo bombers relatively better than dive bombers in campaign in their flexible slots.

Hestia.notes: A repair ship who actually heals, and +1 ammo is very nice for mob. From AA barge to healer AA barge.

Hiei.notes: Assumed to be for battles that last for 10 to 18 seconds ONLY. TRP buff.

Hiei META.notes: Strong debuff but is 70% chance and is partially too late for AFCT/HSFCR BBs.

Hiryuu.notes: Not assumed to be with any Souryuu for 35% AVI.

Hiryuu META.notes: IJN plane is easy to include.

Hiyou META.notes: Not assumed to be with any Junyou.

Honoka.notes: Because of the heal and delayed barrage, Honoka is more suited for mob fleet flagship. She heals two random ships, which is inconsistent in a full fleet of six ships. In a 1:1 low oil fleet, she would always heal herself and the vanguard ship, but Honoka's oil cost of 15 is not suitable for low oil purposes.

Hornet II.notes: Difficult conditions to reach maximum potential against bosses.

Hornet META.notes: Worse than an unactivated Hornet II. First skill barrage misses a lot.

Houshou.notes: Needs to launch airstrike before other main fleet ships. Heals carriers decently and heals battleships poorly.

Houshou META.notes: Needs to launch airstrike before the CVs.

Howe.notes: Desynced BB buffs. Assumed to be with any King George V-class BB, Monarch, or any 3 Royal Navy ships.

Huan Ch'ang.notes: Random buffs cannot be relied on.

Hwah Jah.notes: Chen Hai Pro Plus Max. Top 3 w15 support. Assumes there is another carrier for 10% efficiencies but not any other Dragon Empery ships.

Impero.notes:
Fighter: semi-preload for stagger.
Dive: more damage but very slow.

Implacable.notes: One of the first good freezes in this game, and that’s the main reason you’d use her, because her damage output compared to other rainbow CVs is significantly lower. Unfortunately, she has not aged well, because ships like Lexington ll and Nahkimov have significantly higher damage output. The only advantage Implacable has over those 2 is that there are no conditions for her freeze.

Independence.notes: Without her retrofit, Independence is a very mediocre purple CVL.

Independence is a very good carrier for the main campaign. She has solid damage output, extremely good AA, buffs for carriers in her fleet and in other fleets, and defensive buffs for Eagle Union ships. She's a very good alternative to rainbow carriers in late campaign stages. She's less suited for single-wave bosses because her airstrikes will be desynced from the rest of the fleet and will be unable to take advantage of timed buffs and freezes. She's not the first thing you should buy with core data because she needs a lot of investment to be good, but she is absolutely someone you want to pick up later on. These ratings do not assume there is a Cleveland-class ship.

Indomitable.notes: Illustrious with damage skills. Rocket barrage and 6 fighter slots gives good L/M dmg. One of the best W15/16 support CVs.

Jean Bart.notes: Requires her gun, but really just use a good gun and throw away that part of her skills.

Joffre.notes: Above flag for anti-light. Below flag for anti-heavy or mobbing. Either for anti-medium.

Junyou META.notes: Assumes she equips a Sakura Empire plane but is not sorted with a Hiyou. Not that it would matter with how weak she is.

Kaga.notes: Kaga is a mediocre gold CV. If you really want her, wait until you're further along into the game when you can farm her and Akagi efficiently. These ratings assume she is not with an Akagi for 35% AVI.

Kansas.notes: Kansas is an above average gold BB. She is not forced to play into her skill by using 24s or slower guns. Use standard guns as recommended. Check back in August 2026 (expected) to see how good her Fate Simulation makes her.

Kazan.notes: 40% slow, terrible damage for a 2025 gold BB, but BB healer is interesting

Kearsarge.notes: The only rainbow Aviation Battleship in the game currently, Kearsarge’s loadout is unique among rainbow battleships as she trades her auxiliary gun slot for 4 fighters. This means she’s very lacking in self-defense, making her unsuited for the main campaign (her lack of an aux gun means she can’t kill suicide boats, so you really don’t wanna run her as the flagship, and in campaign carriers tend to be preferred for off-flag, especially in plain heavy content). Her damage against light and medium armor bosses is good and she offers various damage buffs for the main fleet, though bear in mind her reload stat is low for a rainbow BB. The main reason you’d run her is with Eagle Union carriers, so see her other entry. Kearsarge needs an Eagle Union or Northern Parliament main gun and she also needs those factions' fighters in order to apply the shelling buff earlier than the BBs fire.

Kearsarge greatly buffs carriers when there is another Eagle Union main fleet ship and an AA debuff on the boss. Do not bring another source of Air Raid Assistance as Kearsarge's buff already provides that. She forms an anti-light fleet with Yorktown II, Lexington II, and/or Lion. Kearsarge needs an Eagle Union or Northern Parliament main gun and also prefers those factions' fighters for various self-buffs. Fortunately, the current best bossing fighters happen to be of those factions. Do not expect Kearsarge to deal with suicide boats.

Kii.notes: Assumed to be sortied with 3 Sakura Empire ships for 10% self FP and 10% TRP buff. The TRP buff could be useful for EX, with Kii working at level 1.

King George V.notes: Although KGV's unique augment has mutually exclusive effects, it is a definite improvement to her performance. Let's think about the gun first and then the fleet. If KGV is using her historical Quadruple 356mm main gun mount, then she benefits from the existence of another Royal Navy ally. If KGV is not using the Quadruple 356mm, then she benefits from there being no other Royal Navy ship. Note that the converse is not necessarily true; if there is another Royal Navy ship, the appropriate rainbow guns are still better than the Quadruple 356mm. If you have enough of the appropriate rainbow guns to equip other BBs as well as KGV, then KGV should always use those guns. If you're poor and still want to use KGV, then the Quadruple 356mm is a decent option.

Klaudia Valentz.notes: Klaudia is a solid healer. Compared to Unicorn, Klaudia lacks preloaded damage, and the total amount of healing is less.

Kongou μ.notes: Assumes there is another muse ship or normal ship with special gear.

Langley II.notes: Requires carrier fleet. Needs to launch airstrike before other main fleet ships.

Lexington II.notes: These ratings assume that there is no AA debuff and that there are fewer than 3 Eagle Union ships. Lexington II applies a 40% slow under these assumptions. See her other entry for upgrading the slow to a freeze. Lexington ll is one of the best ships in the game against light armor enemies and has good damage against medium armor as well. She also has very useful utility in the main campaign. If your fleet shoots down 17 aircraft or she loses 25% of her HP, she gains 1 stack of her blue skill, and once she gains 4 stacks, she can reduce the damage your main fleet takes from enemy aircraft by 100%. This benefit is not relevant in mob battles but is relevant in campaign boss battles.

These ratings assume there are 3 Eagle Union ships, including another Eagle Union main fleet ship. She will usually be with Kearsarge, Yorktown II, or both. Lion can substitute for one of them. There must also be an AA debuffer in the fleet, which Yorktown II or some vanguard ships provide. Lexington II can then provide a 4-second freeze for the fleet, removing the need to run Implacable or Nahkimov, who have notably worse anti-light damage. This forms a top anti-light boss fleet that can also fight medium armor decently.

Lion.notes: One of the most broken ships in the game currently, Lion delivers the highest overall solo damage of any ship in the game. Furthermore, she applies a permanent 10% damage debuff to any enemy afflicted by her burn, which is also permanent. And to add the cherry on top, she is one of the few BBs with salvo capacity +1, making her quicker to reload her main guns in practice compared to other BBs. While she may not be the absolute best choice for every specific niche or composition, her raw output is so immense that she consistently features in the top one to five meta comps for all relevant content. No other rainbow ship dominates the game quite like she does; she is an absolute top-priority investment.

Little Formidable.notes: High chance for decent to strong slow.

Little Illustrious.notes: After 4 years, her skill is no longer bugged.

Little Renown.notes: Assume there are multiple HMS ships.

Long Island.notes: Needs to launch airstrike before other main fleet ships. Aug's eff is bugged, only gives +1.5%.

Luna.notes: Luna has two 50% reload time airstrikes, so she is not a true stagger from other carriers like Independence is. The first airstrike is staggered but later ones may be close to Unicorn. She can be used for farming fast in Operation Siren while not being terrible at Strongholds or bosses, but overall Independence just does everything better.

Maryland.notes: Without her retrofit, Maryland is just a mediocre purple BB.

Maryland is a solid battleship for new players. Note that she does need her retrofit. Maryland's debuff for 10% EVA is something, but it's not enough for a 1 in Offense Buff. Her retrofit skill is bugged to give 4.5% HIT instead of 12%.

Massachusetts.notes: Needs to NOT use her unique augment against light armor enemies. Augment gives ~26% more damage for M/H.

Masséna.notes: Preload, high light damage, can chain up to three 88% chance barrages.

Mecklenburg.notes: One of the best all-around rainbow BBs in the game currently. She has good damage against light armor and outstanding damage against medium and heavy armor. She's one of the few BBs with salvo capacity +1, making her quicker to reload her main guns in practice compared to other BBs. She has a 5% buff for the fleet for 8s when she fires, so she prefers firing first, but 5% may not beat good sync if she can't easily fire first. Her skills do give her a preference to be sortied with Bismarck Zwei (see Mecklenburg's other entry), but this is very much a case of nice to have than a necessity for her to perform well.

One of the best all-around rainbow BBs in the game currently. She has good damage against light armor and outstanding damage against medium and heavy armor. She's one of the few BBs with salvo capacity +1, making her quicker to reload her main guns in practice compared to other BBs. She has a 5% buff for the fleet for 8s when she fires, so she prefers firing first, but 5% may not beat good sync if she can't easily fire first. When synced with Bismarck Zwei, Mecklenburg gains 15% RLD and gives the fleet another up to 5% more damage.

Mikasa.notes: Mikasa is bad at everything besides buffing BBs through a 60% chance and buffing Sakura Empire ships. These ratings assume she is being used to buff non-Sakura BBs. For EX, she should be used purely as a buff bot at level 1. She is also the lowest power BB for filling requirements, beating common rarity BBs.

Mikasa is bad at everything besides buffing BBs through a 60% chance and buffing Sakura Empire ships. These ratings assume she is being used to buff Musashi. For EX, she should be used purely as a buff bot at level 1. She is also the lowest power BB for filling requirements, beating common rarity BBs.

Monarch.notes: Decent slow, small EVA debuff, 100% chance barrage.

Musashi.notes: Musashi is one of the best battleships in late campaign stages thanks to her ability to tank damage for the main fleet. If she’s equipped appropriately and sortied with the right ships, she can drastically improve the survivability of your main fleet. However, her skill can also get her killed more quickly if appropriate measures are not taken (i.e. giving her defensive gear like a Rudder or Fire Extinguisher and pairing her with targeted healers like Cowpens/Aquila or flagship defenders like Z52/Porter). Outside of the main campaign, against single target bosses, her performance is somewhat lacking relative to newer rainbow BBs due to her low reload stat and her requirement for a Sakura Empire main gun.

Musashi-chan.notes: Unlike her mom, she's not limited to a Sakura Empire main gun.

Nagato.notes: Nagato has a decent offensive buff for Sakura Empire ships and a huge offensive buff for Sakura Empire carriers. These ratings assume she's not with any Sakura main fleet ships, and her buff for Sakura vanguard ships is usually not significant.

Nagato has a decent offensive buff for Sakura Empire ships and a huge offensive buff for Sakura Empire carriers. These ratings assume she's buffing two rainbow IJN CVs, which include Shinano, Hakuhou, Amagi(CV), and Hakuryuu. The 20% reload buff enables these CVs to complete 4 airstrikes in META Showdown (80 seconds) without heavily griefing their airplane choices. As a BB, Nagato also enables bringing Trafalgar, or other buffers who require a BB flagship, in the Sakura CV fleet. Note that without a freeze, such a fleet is only good if timed to the boss's natural stop times.

Nagato META.notes: Assume there are zero IJN ships in fleet.

Nagisa.notes: In bossing, Nagisa should fire before the other main fleet ships to apply a 30% slow and 10% EVA debuff.

Nelson.notes: Without her retrofit, Nelson is just a mediocre purple BB.
Nelson is a solid battleship for new players. Note that she needs to be retrofitted and using her flags auxiliary gear obtained from Memento.

Nevada META.notes: Quite bad. But BB RLD +1 very good!

New Jersey.notes: New Jersey is a solid all-around BB, but she's been powercrept in just about every metric and now sits at the bottom end of rainbow BBs. If you like her, then use her. But from a purely objective standpoint, with the constant influx of new rainbow BBs, it's very difficult to justify spending rainbow Bulins on her.

Nina Friede.notes: Not assumed, but slight bonus for having another Atelier Yumia ship.

North Carolina.notes: Requires a fuse AA gun and requires enemy airplanes.

Nyotengu.notes: Some bombs delayed by 5 seconds after her airstrike could be useful in mobbing...if she manages to kill anything with her poor stats. To add insult to injury, Nyotengu's unique augment only improves her damage by 9%.

Origami Tobiichi.notes: 8% more damage vs enemies with < 43 speed.

Oumi.notes: A gold BB with unusually high potential damage output due to her long-range secondary guns. If the boss sits in range of her secondary guns for extended amounts of time, the guns do noticeably high damage. She is still good even if she isn't able to bring her secondaries in range.

Owari.notes: Was the best gold BB for 2 years, from Sep 2023 to Aug 2025.

Pearl.notes: Does not have access to good guns and auxiliaries.

Perseus.notes: Perseus is a solid healer, but she is worse than Unicorn in most aspects, especially in long fights due to the massive penalty on Perseus's airstrike cooldown.

Peter Strasser.notes: Assumed to be with 4 Iron Blood ships for reduced Iron Blood carrier reload times. A 3s freeze means her own TBs still miss.

Prince of Wales.notes: Needs 3 other USS/HMS ships, and buffs USS/HMS carriers.

Queen Anne's Revenge.notes: Does not have access to good guns and auxiliaries. Assumed to be with another Tempesta ship. Buffs Tempesta ships.

Queen Elizabeth.notes: Assumed to be buffing multiple HMS ships. So she is bad either way.

Queen Elizabeth META.notes: Assumes there are 2 other META ships.

Raffaello.notes: One of the best battleship in late campaign thanks to her ability to shield and heal your vanguards, effectively making her a pseudo healer on top of good damage output. However, her performance against bosses is wanting thanks to her relatively low damage output relative to other rainbow BBs.

Renown.notes: Assumes there is another HMS ship for +30% barrage chance.

Repulse META.notes: Requires an HMS gear, easy to do.

Richelieu.notes: Richelieu is the Iris Orthodoxy (Iris Libre + Vichya) faction buffer. These ratings assume that she is buffing 1 or 2 other Iris Orthodoxy ships. She is usable without other Iris ships but loses the Offense Buff bonus.
Richelieu is the Iris Orthodoxy (Iris Libre + Vichya) faction buffer. These ratings assume that she is buffing Alsace. Richelieu can be max level or level 1 in EX.

Rodney META.notes: Great gold BB who is good at dealing with suicide boats with her constant Little Seven and blocking summons.

Saratoga.notes: Without her retrofit, Saratoga loses some damage but still fulfills her role of continuous AoE bombing. Using her unique augment, Saratoga offers continuous damage with mini-airstrikes every 10 seconds. This, combined with her dive bomber-focused loadout, makes her more suited for campaign than single-wave bosses. Even without her unique augment, she is still strong for new players due to how good purple Helldivers are.

Using her unique augment, Saratoga offers continuous damage with mini-airstrikes every 10 seconds. This, combined with her dive bomber-focused loadout, makes her more suited for campaign than single-wave bosses.

Scharnhorst META.notes: Assumes there is another META or Iron Blood ship for +12% FP.

Seydlitz.notes: Assumes there is another Iron Blood ship for +18% FP and RLD.

Shangri-La.notes: Slightly stronger in long battles, approaching a 70% Enterprise.

Shinano.notes: Shinano has minor buffs for everyone. She prefers 3 Sakura Empire ships, including herself, to give +15% AVI and HIT to all Sakura carriers, including herself. With strong torpedo bombers and weak fighters, she leans to anti-heavy bossing. These ratings assume that she has 2 Sakura friends who aren't carriers.

Shinano has minor buffs for everyone. She requires 3 Sakura Empire ships, including herself, to give +15% AVI and HIT to all Sakura carriers, including herself. Assumed to be with Amagi(CV) or Hakuhou. Shinano greatly buffs them while having respectable damage herself. With strong torpedo bombers and weak fighters, the whole fleet is good against heavy armor bosses.
Note: When this ship is sortied with Amagi CV, the latter's damage buff to torpedoes from Sakura Empire ships makes converging torpedo bombers better than BF-109Gs against medium armor (assuming they hit the boss reliably) and parallel torpedo bombers relatively better than dive bombers in campaign in their flexible slots.

Shinano-chan.notes: Note: When this ship is sortied with Amagi CV, the latter's damage buff to torpedoes from Sakura Empire ships makes converging torpedo bombers better than BF-109Gs against medium armor (assuming they hit the boss reliably) and parallel torpedo bombers relatively better than dive bombers in campaign in their flexible slots.

Shizuku.notes: Shizuku buffs fleet FP, AA, and EVA. Do not be baited into using worse longer-reload guns just for a tiny increase in these buffs. She does have a 100% chance barrage on main gun salvo, so using slower guns will also nerf that damage. Shizuku also has various minor bits of healing that aren't tied to her main gun salvos. The minor bits are a mix of targeting random and targeting lowest percentage HP, and they add up to about 4% per main fleet ship and 13% per vanguard ship in expectation for an 80 second battle (slightly less for typical 50-70 second late campaign mob battles), assuming a vanguard ship usually has the lowest percentage HP remaining. The small AA and EVA buffs further boost her whole-fleet protection. This is quite solid in both mobbing and bossing, though of course Shizuku does not excuse Unicorn from your mob fleet. Lastly, not mentioned in the skill text is that her barrage has a chance to apply a Richelieu burn, which decreases enemy FP, TRP, and AVI by 5%.

Shouhou.notes: Shouhou without retrofit is outclassed by Unicorn in every way. Needs to launch airstrike before other main fleet ships.
Shouhou with retrofit is outclassed by even a partially retrofitted Unicorn. Needs to launch airstrike before other main fleet ships.

Shoukaku.notes: Needs to launch airstrike before other main fleet ships. It's not assumed here, but Shoukaku does 8% more damage if with Zuikaku.

Souryuu.notes: Not assumed to be with a Hiryuu for +35% AVI.

Souryuu META.notes: Assumed to equip a Sakura Empire plane OR be sortied with any Hiryuu.

Sovetskaya Rossiya.notes: Assumes there is another Northern Parliament ship. Prefers more Northern Parliament or Dragon Empery ships. Augment gives ~25% more damage.

Sovetsky Soyuz.notes: When Soyuz is sortied with at least one other battleship, she buffs her own damage, crit rate, and reload by 10%. She’s very strong and flexible, but she has overall fallen behind newer rainbow battleships.

When sortied with two carriers, Soyuz offers a sizeable buff for the carriers at the cost of some of her own damage. She has particularly strong synergy with Admiral Nahkimov, though this pairing is not accounted for in these ratings. See her pairing entry with Nakhimov.

When Soyuz is sortied with at least one other battleship, she buffs her own damage, crit rate, and reload by 10%. When she’s sortied with 2 carriers, she loses these self buffs but buffs the accuracy and damage output of your carriers by 10%. She has particularly strong synergy with Admiral Nahkimov as Soyuz can proc the latter’s freeze with her barrage, which slows the enemies hit by it.

Strasbourg.notes: Assumes there are 2 other Vichya Dominion ships. Offense Buff reaches 1 only if there are 4 to 6 MNF ships.

São Martinho.notes: Does not have access to good guns and auxiliaries.

Taihou.notes: Needs to finish reloading before other main fleet ships launch airstrikes or land salvos.

Taihou META.notes: Taihou sidegrade, better stats but worse barrage(s) and no buff.

Taihou μ.notes: Assumed to have up to 3 other muse ships in the fleet. Ships can equip certain muse gear to be counted as muse ships.

Tamaki.notes: Tamaki's extended secondary gun range of 80 is good for dealing with Bombing Ships in all of campaign and Kagerou Productions in Chapter 14. However, 80 range does not reach 99% of bosses. The guaranteed Armor Break on barrage hit is not limited to heavy armor, giving her +1 Offense Buff against light and medium armor bosses.

Theseus.notes: Decent everywhere but is a CVL, benefitting less from cats.

Thüringen.notes: Assumed to be buffing multiple KMS ships.

Ticonderoga.notes: Defensive skills good for campaign. Rocket barrage is ok for light/medium boss DPS.

Tirpitz.notes: Assumes there is no other BB/BC, though Iron Blood BB/BCs are ok.

Ulrich von Hutten.notes: Ulrich von Hutten (UvH) is a solid all-around BB, but she's been powercrept in just about every metric and now sits at the bottom end of rainbow BBs. She has a unique gimmick of firing twice as often as most other rainbow BBs when she's placed off flag, but this often works against her. Half of her salvos will miss common timed buffs or debuffs from the rest of your fleet. You could solve this by running her as the flagship, but her overall damage output is even worse as flagship. Spamming salvos twice as often also exposes her faster in Chapter 14, making her likely to take one for the team prematurely. Her main gun damage reduction when off flag also stacks additively with the out of ammo debuff, meaning she only deals 5% main gun damage when the fleet she's in is out of ammo and she's placed off flag. If you like her, then use her. But from a purely objective standpoint, with the constant influx of new rainbow BBs, it's very difficult to justify spending rainbow Bulins on her.

Unicorn.notes: Without her retrofit, Unicorn is a decent but underwhelming healer. Her retrofit is a noticeable upgrade.

As one of the best healers in the game, Unicorn is practically an auto pick in your mob fleet for the vast majority of your time pushing content. She does fall off a bit in the very late game as her low damage starts to show, but she remains a very strong choice for mobbing. You can obtain her from the Guild Shop right after you finish the tutorial, and she is a must pick-up for new players.

Unryuu.notes: Unryuu has a 50% semi-preload, making her first airstrike earlier than Independence's would be. However, Independence still enjoys various advantages.

Valiant.notes: A 50% damage barrage, and a debuff that can miss and doesn't apply to the first salvo.

Vanguard.notes: A support oriented rainbow Battleship, Vanguard’s own damage is really low to the point where quite a few gold BBs do more damage than her. However, she compensates for her low damage with very strong damage buffs/debuffs. This makes her a solid choice for single-wave bosses. Her low personal damage holds her back in late campaign stages despite her high AA relative to other BBs. Also note that compared to most other ships, she scales far more heavily with how good (or bad) the rest of the fleet is.

Vestal.notes: Minor heals both inside and outside battle, and +1 ammo is very nice for mob.

Vestal META.notes: Minor heals both inside and outside battle, and +1 ammo is very nice for mob.

Victorious.notes: Assumed to be fighting BB bosses only.

Vittorio Veneto.notes: Assumed to be buffing multiple Sardegna Empire ships.

Volga.notes: Volga is a decent healer with higher damage. Her heals scale with her own max HP rather than the target’s, which makes her better at healing low HP ships like DDs but worse for main fleet ships and cruisers. The total amount of healing she provides is relatively low, and its targeting is a bit random. She's a decent option if you're lacking healers, but there are better ships.

Warspite.notes: Without her retrofit, Warspite needs her unique augment to be a below average gold BB. With neither retrofit nor unique augment, she's one of the worst gold BBs in the game.

Warspite is a REAL rainbow ship now with her augment. But she is still among the worst rainbow BBs because she has no fleet buffs and has significant staggered barrages that miss moving bosses. Her retrofit is VERY expensive, and she needs her unique augment on top of it.

Washington.notes: Her sweeping barrage has short range and fails to hit most enemies. Assumed to not be with South Dakota.

Wasp.notes: Lowest power CV for filling requirements. Assumed to not be with a Royal Navy ship, though it doesn't matter either way.

West Virginia.notes: Without her retrofit, West Virginia is just a mediocre purple BB.
Her 70% barrage with debuffs arrives somewhat late even if she is first to fire. Barely gets a 1 for Offense Buff.

Yamashiro.notes: Fully retrofitting Fusou and Yamashiro makes them much weaker. But they're bottom tier with or without retrofit. If you want maximum performance from them, retrofit until the Modernization node, do not complete Modernization. For collection percentage or historical reasons, just complete the retrofit.

Yamashiro META.notes: Should use any Sakura Empire gear for 10% more damage. Contrary to what the game says, she does 10% more damage to enemies hit by her barrage, and the 10% damage is not limited to the barrage.

Yorktown II.notes: These ratings assume that Yorktown II has an Eagle Union airplane equipped and is sortied with 2 other Eagle ships, but that she is not with Kearsarge or Yorktown/Essex-class. Yorktown II is one of the best ships in the game against light armor enemies with excellent damage against medium armor as well. She has a unique ability which allows her to decrease the airstrike cooldowns of Yorktown and Essex class carriers, so check out her other entry. She also wants to be sortied with 2 other Eagle Union ships to proc a 15% AVI and HIT buff for herself.

Yorktown II requires an Eagle Union airplane and 3 Eagle Union ships in the fleet. Strong fighters, weak TBs, and a Skyraider barrage make her good against light bosses and poor against heavy bosses. These ratings assume that all conditions are met and she is with Kearsarge, Lexington II, and/or Essex. She has a unique ability which allows her to decrease the airstrike cooldowns of Yorktown and Essex class carriers in her fleet by 10% when she launches her own airstrike, which is very useful for syncing your Yorktown and Essex class ships and for completing their 4th airstrikes in META Showdowns. The window of 8% or 10% of the reload time makes syncing them extremely easy. This skill is also why she prefers to launch first in bossing, otherwise the fleet gets very desynced.

Yorktown META.notes: 10% AA/EVA debuff, buffs any Yorktown, buffs Framework of Logic.

Yoshino.notes: Pseudo-healer with high damage but is squishy herself. Random slows.

Yumi.notes: The 2 to 3 second freeze happens too early, so some TBs will miss.

Yumia Liessfeldt.notes: Endemeteo for CV boss dmg. And/or Superior Grimoire for stagger or extra airstrike. Or Granshine for campaign.
Yumia can bring Panacea Sphere as the only item effect to get 2.5% vanguard heal every 8s. Because there is no main fleet healing, you will need a fleet with good AA or anti-shelling.

Zeppy.notes: Assumes there are many KMS ships.

Zuihou.notes: Zuihou is a great healer but has very poor damage. Her vanguard heals scale with her own max HP rather than the target’s, which makes her better at healing low HP ships like DDs but worse for cruisers. Her main fleet heals scale with the target's max HP, letting Zuihou heal them decently effectively. She’s a very useful ship to have for late campaign stages, but she has been powercept by Cowpens.

Zuikaku.notes: Prefers 3 Sakura Empire ships. Ramp up time favors longer battles. These ratings assume she is with 3 Sakura ships but not with Shoukaku, missing out on 20% AVI.
